memory_policy.default_context: -c 0 (default) = model n_ctx_train. --fit is on by default: if the projected use exceeds free device memory minus --fit-target (1024 MiB/device), an UNSET context is lowered (floor --fit-ctx 4096) and layers/experts are moved to CPU. A context set with -c is never changed.
memory_policy.details: n_ctx is the TOTAL KV cell count, padded to 256. Unified KV (default when -np is auto): one pool of n_ctx cells shared by every slot, and each slot may use up to n_ctx. With an explicit -np N and no -kvu, n_ctx is split into N streams of n_ctx/N. What scales with the slot count (n_seq_max): the recurrent/SSM state (F32, one per sequence) and, with unified KV, the SWA window (n_swa*n_seq_max + n_ubatch). The whole KV is allocated at context creation. --cache-ram (default 8192 MiB) caps a separate host-RAM prompt cache.

attention_support.details: The SWA cache is sized min(n_ctx_seq, n_swa*(unified ? n_seq_max : 1) + n_ubatch), padded to 256. --swa-full makes it full size. MLA stores only K = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim per layer (has_v = !is_mla). Hybrid architectures include qwen3next, qwen35, qwen35moe, kimi-linear, minimax-01 (linear), plus jamba, falcon-h1, granitehybrid, nemotron_h, lfm2, plamo2 (SSM). mamba, mamba2 and rwkv6/7 are pure recurrent. The recurrent state is F32 regardless of -ctk.

engines.offload: -ngl N|auto|all (default auto, resolved by --fit); -ot '<regex>=<buffer>' tensor overrides; --cpu-moe (all experts on CPU) and --n-cpu-moe N (experts of the first N layers on CPU); --n-cpu-ffn N (dense FFN); -nkvo keeps the KV cache in host RAM.
engines.overhead_notes: Printed by llama_memory_breakdown_print as model + context + compute per device. Documented example (tools/fit-params/README.md): Qwen3-30B-A3B f16, -c 4096, RTX 4090 shows 17904 MiB model + 384 MiB context + 898 MiB compute. The compute buffer grows with n_ubatch (default 512). --fit keeps a 1024 MiB free margin per device by default.
engines.notes: llama.cpp now ships semver releases (v0.4.1, 2026-09-14) next to its nightly bNNNNN builds; the pin above is the semver tag. The README bpw table was measured on Llama-3.1-8B, while quantize.cpp's option strings cite Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B. Mixes keep 1D tensors (norms) unquantized and put output.weight (or tied token_embd) at Q6_K for most k-quants.

memory_policy.default_context: num_ctx comes from the request, then the Modelfile, then OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH. Without any of those it is VRAM-tiered on total VRAM across GPUs (minus OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD): >=47 GiB => 262144, >=23 GiB => 32768, otherwise 4096. It is capped at the model's training context. On a load OOM, an automatic context is retried once at the next lower tier (32768, then 4096).
memory_policy.default_parallel: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL default 1. Forced to 1 for embeddings and for model families mllama, qwen3vl, qwen3vlmoe, qwen35, qwen35moe, qwen3next, lfm2, lfm2moe, nemotron_h, nemotron_h_moe, nemotron_h_omni.
memory_policy.details: llama-server is launched with -c num_ctx*num_parallel and -np num_parallel, without -kvu, so KV = num_ctx x parallel (FAQ: 'Required RAM will scale by OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL * OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH'). Automatic num_batch (passed as -b and -ub): 2048 when effective ctx > 32768, 1024 when > 4096, else 512 (512/256 on CUDA without FA). It steps down when predicted VRAM is too close to free memory. OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS default 3 x GPUs (3 on CPU).

attention_support.details: All GGUF models run in the upstream llama-server subprocess (LLAMA_CPP_VERSION = b10760), so KV behaviour follows llama.cpp (SWA window cache, MLA K-only, hybrid recurrent state). These flags were verified against llama.cpp v0.4.1 source, not re-read at b10760. Ollama passes no --swa-full. Hybrid families run with num_parallel forced to 1.

engines.offload: Automatic: Ollama omits -ngl by default and llama-server's --fit picks the GPU layer split. The num_gpu option maps to -ngl N (0 = CPU only). `ollama ps` PROCESSOR shows the CPU/GPU split.
engines.overhead_notes: The scheduler reserves MinimumMemory per GPU (457 MiB non-Metal, 512 MiB Metal) plus OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD (user bytes, default 0). Its memory prediction adds a batch surcharge (768 MiB at num_batch 1024, 2 GiB at 2048) and evicts other models when the prediction exceeds 80% of free memory. PredictServerVRAM is only a planning estimate: GGUF file size + 2*layers*kv_heads*head_dim*ctx*2 bytes (f16, no SWA/MLA awareness).
engines.notes: v0.34.1 is still at rc2, so v0.34.0 is the latest stable. Ollama's in-house GGML runner is gone: 'All GGML models are served via the upstream llama-server subprocess.' docs/faq.mdx still says the default context is 4096, which contradicts context-length.mdx and routes.go (VRAM-tiered).

memory_policy.default_parallel: Max Concurrent Predictions default 4 (llama.cpp engine), Unified KV Cache on by default
memory_policy.details: 0.4.0 notes say 4 parallel slots with unified KV 'should result in no additional memory overhead'. With useUnifiedKvCache=false each prediction gets the full context 'at the cost of using more memory'. Guardrails: the loader estimates memory from context length, GPU offload, flash attention and vision; it warns or blocks loads that would exceed resources and can be overridden. `lms load --estimate-only` prints 'Estimated GPU Memory / Total Memory' and whether it 'passes guardrails'. The guardrail levels and thresholds are not documented in the fetched sources. gpuStrictVramCap caps offload at detected VRAM. autoFit picks context and placement (SDK doc: 'only available when using Bionic'); the Bionic 1.1.2 changelog adds `lms load --auto`, and the link between the two is inferred.

attention_support.details: Closed-source runtimes. The llama.cpp engine presumably inherits upstream behaviour, but the upstream commit and flags such as --swa-full are not documented, so these are null.

engines.offload: lms load --gpu 0-1|off|max (fraction of layers on GPU; default automatic); offloadKVCacheToGpu (false = KV in RAM, llama.cpp engine only); gpuStrictVramCap; numCpuExpertLayersRatio in the SDK (0.3.24 notes).
engines.notes: The app is closed source and no license text was fetched, so license is null. Flash Attention defaults to on for the CUDA (0.3.31), Vulkan and Metal (0.3.32) llama.cpp engines. The default context is unverified: 0.3.2 cut it from 8K to 4K, 0.3.24 added an app-wide 'default context length' setting, and the current value is not in the fetched docs.

memory_policy.default_context: max_model_len defaults to the model config's maximum. -1/'auto' picks the largest length that fits. Startup fails if the KV pool cannot hold one max_model_len request.
memory_policy.default_parallel: max_num_seqs 256 (GPUs < 70 GiB, or A100), 1024 (>= 70 GiB non-A100 and >= 160 GiB); CPU 128 x world_size for the API server
memory_policy.details: requested = total_GPU_memory x gpu_memory_utilization (per instance, default 0.92). KV pool = requested - (weights + peak activations from a profile run at max_num_batched_tokens + non-torch memory) - CUDA graph estimate. The graph estimate is profiled and subtracted by default (VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1). The pool is allocated up front and shared by all sequences as paged blocks (block_size 16). kv_cache_memory_bytes overrides the fraction. Startup errors if free memory < requested.

attention_support.details: The hybrid KV cache manager gives sliding-window layers only the most recent sliding_window tokens. If disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager is set (default decided by environment/config), SWA layers are allocated like full attention. MLAAttentionSpec uses num_kv_heads=1, head_size = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim, and no separate V. Mamba/GDN state uses mamba_cache_dtype (default = model). Model files present: qwen3_next, qwen3_5, jamba, falcon_h1, granitemoehybrid, nemotron_h, mamba2.

engines.offload: --cpu-offload-gb N ('virtual' extra GPU memory for weights; needs a fast CPU-GPU interconnect); --kv-offloading-size GiB (KV to CPU, native or lmcache backend). There is no llama.cpp-style per-layer GPU/CPU split flag.
engines.overhead_notes: Not a constant. CUDA-graph memory is profiled and deducted inside the gpu_memory_utilization budget, and the log suggests an equivalent utilization. Peak activation is measured by a dummy forward pass at max_num_batched_tokens (2048 for the API server on < 70 GiB GPUs). CPU backend: VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE, or auto-sized when unset.
engines.notes: The default gpu_memory_utilization is 0.92 at v0.29.0, not the long-documented 0.9. Several docs pages (metrics.md, usage_stats.md, benchmark examples) still show 0.9.

memory_policy.default_context: context_length defaults to the model config.json value
memory_policy.default_parallel: max_running_requests unset (bounded by pool); cuda-graph decode max_bs by GPU size: <20 GiB 8, <35 GiB 24, <60 GiB 32, <90/<160 GiB 256, else 512 (tp<4)
memory_policy.details: mem_fraction_static = (weights + KV pool)/GPU memory. When unset it is computed as (gpu_mem_MB - reserved_mem)/gpu_mem_MB, where reserved_mem (MB) = 512 + 1.5*max(chunked_prefill_size, 2048) + tp*pp/8*1024 + graph reserve (2*decode max_bs + 8*len(prefill graph bs), or 1.5 GiB for MLA), with a floor of 10 GiB on GPUs > 60 GiB. Default chunked_prefill_size is 2048 below 35 GiB, 4096 below 60 GiB, 8192 below 160 GiB, else 16384. Fallback 0.88 when GPU memory is unknown; VLMs get a further adjustment. max_total_tokens is derived from that pool and shared across requests (radix cache).

attention_support.details: The hybrid SWA memory pool (on by default; --disable-hybrid-swa-memory) sizes SWA-layer token capacity at swa_full_tokens_ratio (default 0.8) of full-layer capacity. It is ratio-based, not a strict window. MLATokenToKVPool kv_cache_dim = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim. HybridLinearKVPool + MambaPool serve GDN/Mamba (mamba_full_memory_ratio 0.9; mamba_ssm_dtype from the model config, float32/bf16/fp16). Model files: qwen3_5, qwen3_next, nemotron_h, falcon_h1, gpt_oss, gemma3.

engines.offload: --cpu-offload-gb N (RAM reserved for weight offload) with offload_group_size/offload_num_in_group/offload_prefetch_step. No -ngl-style layer count.
engines.overhead_notes: reserved_mem heuristic above: activations 1.5 MB per chunked-prefill token, 512 MB constant metadata, plus graph buffers. SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING (default False) would size KV after graph capture instead, reserving only 1536 MB + parallel slack.
engines.notes: mem_fraction_static has no fixed default: it is None and resolved per GPU size, so 'fraction' is null. For a 24 GiB card the formula gives about 0.83 with prefill CUDA graphs reserved (4096 MB) and about 0.85 without (3760 MB). That figure is derived, not printed in docs.

memory_policy.default_context: No preset limit. The cache grows with actual tokens. --max-kv-size N switches to a fixed-size rotating cache.
memory_policy.details: Each sequence owns its cache, so memory is the sum of the tokens in flight (worst case = concurrency x context). On Metal, generation raises the wired limit to max_recommended_working_set_size and warns when the model exceeds 90% of it. README: raise it with `sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=N` (macOS 15+). The server prompt cache holds 10 distinct KV caches by default (--prompt-cache-size), optionally capped with --prompt-cache-bytes.

attention_support.details: gemma3_text and gpt_oss put SWA layers on RotatingKVCache(max_size=sliding_window). deepseek_v3 caches kv_latent (kv_lora_rank) + k_pe (rope dim) instead of full K/V. qwen3_5 linear layers use ArraysCache(size=2) (fixed-size state). Model files exist for nemotron_h, falcon_h1, jamba, granitemoehybrid, kimi_linear, mamba2, qwen3_next; their cache classes were not individually inspected.

engines.offload: None: unified memory, no GPU/CPU layer split. Models above the wired limit page and slow down.

kv_cache_dtypes.requires: Not a dtype. Evicted KV blocks go to SSD as safetensors and are restored on a prefix hit. It does not shrink the RAM KV of active requests.

memory_policy.default_context: The model's native context when discovered (optional max_context_window_policy caps it). Fallback max_context_window = 32768 when unknown; per-model override max_context_window.
memory_policy.details: Hard ceiling = min(static, dynamic, metal_cap). static = total RAM - tier reserve: safe 8 GiB, balanced 6 GiB (default tier), aggressive 4 GiB, custom 2 GiB; machines < 24 GiB always reserve 4 GiB. dynamic = oMLX phys + free + inactive + active x (0.2/0.5/0.8), or the user GB for custom (--memory-guard-gb). metal_cap = iogpu.wired_limit_mb if set, else max_recommended_working_set_size. Soft watermark (tier: 0.85/0.90/0.925/0.85) pauses admission and evicts LRU models; hard 0.95 aborts in-flight work. KV is paged (block-based, prefix sharing, CoW) and grows on demand.

attention_support.details: Models come from the pinned mlx-lm commit (RotatingKVCache for SWA, latent cache for DeepSeek V3, ArraysCache for Qwen3.5 GDN at v0.31.3), but oMLX's paged cache path was not verified to preserve window-only storage. GDN state support is explicit: gdn_snapshot_storage auto|ssd_sidecar|embedded, gdn_sidecar_precision fp32. README mentions rotating-KV limits only for distributed mode.

engines.offload: No weight offload (unified memory). KV blocks tier to SSD (cold) and optionally to a RAM hot cache.
engines.overhead_notes: Static reserve per tier (above). _HOT_CACHE_RESERVATION_SLACK_BYTES = 512 MiB. No runtime compute-buffer figure is documented.
engines.notes: The README says the process memory limit defaults to 'system RAM - 8GB', but code at v0.6.4 defaults to tier 'balanced' = RAM - 6 GiB (8 GiB is the 'safe' tier). MemorySettings.soft_threshold defaults to 0.85 while the enforcer's balanced tier uses 0.90 (a saved 0.85 counts as legacy). v0.7.0.dev2 exists but is a pre-release.

memory_policy.details: Cache(max_num_tokens) is allocated at model load in 256-token pages and shared by all jobs ('total number of tokens that can be allocated across concurrent jobs; seq_len * batch_size <= max_num_tokens'). Recurrent models reserve max_batch_size state slots (+ max_history).

attention_support.details: cache/mla.py stores ckv (kv_lora_rank) + kpe (qk_rope_head_dim) per token. README lists Qwen 3-Next and Qwen 3.5 (GDN) and NemotronH, with cache/recurrent.py. SWA models (Gemma 2/3, GPT-OSS) are supported, but whether SWA layers get window-sized cache was not verified. The docstring says layer_type only affects global-attention layers.

engines.offload: Multi-GPU layer split / tensor parallel; experimental -mcl/--moe_cpu_offload N runs routed experts of the first N MoE layers on CPU (layer-split mode only).
engines.overhead_notes: EXL3_QC_STAGING=1 (default) reserves an fp16 scratch of 2*max_num_tokens*num_kv_heads*head_dim elements per device when a quantized cache is used (docs: ~4 GB at 1M tokens, 8 kv heads x 128). EXL3_QC_STAGING=0 removes it.
engines.notes: The README links doc/exl3.md, which does not exist at v1.5.0. TensorRT-LLM (latest stable tag v1.2.1; 1.3.0 still at rc26) was not researched, because the brief allowed one NVIDIA-only engine and ExLlamaV3 verified cleanly.
